title: CRLR/457/2022 of SOMNATH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 457 of 2022
Somnath ....Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ..... Respondent
Mr. Navneet Kaushik, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The instant revision is preferred against the
following:-
 (A) judgment and order dated 31.10.2018,
passed in Criminal Case No.207 of 2017, State Vs.
Somnath, by the court of 1st Additional Civil Judge
(Junior Division)/ Judicial Magistrate, Roorkee, District
Haridwar ("the case"). By it, the revisionist has been
convicted under Sections 279, 337, 338, 427 & 304-A
IPC and sentenced as hereunder:-
(i) Under Section 279 IPC, 6 months rigorous
imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 200/-. In
default of payment of fine, rigorous
imprisonment for a further period of 10
days.

2
(ii) Under Section 337 IPC, 6 months rigorous
imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 200. In
default of payment of fine, rigorous
imprisonment for a further period of 10
days.
(iii) Under Section 338 IPC, 2 years rigorous
imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 500/-. In
default of payment of fine, rigorous
imprisonment for a further period of one
month.
(iv) Under Section 304-A IPC, 2 years rigorous
imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 500/-. In
default of payment of fine, rigorous
imprisonment for a further period of one
month. And,
(v) Under Section 427 IPC, 2 years rigorous
imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 500/-. In
default of payment of fine, rigorous
imprisonment for a further period of one
month.
 (B) Judgment and order dated
05.08.2022, passed in Criminal Appeal No.241 of 2018,
Somnath Vs. State of Uttarakhand, by the court of 1st

3
Additonal Sessions Judge, Roorkee, District Haridwar
("the appeal"), by which, the appeal has been dismissed
and the conviction and sentence passed in the case, has
been upheld.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. Facts necessary to appreciate the
controversy, briefly stated, are as follows: According to
the case, on 07.07.2000, at 7:30 P.M., the revisionist,
while driving a bus bearing registration no. UP-07J-9239
("the bus") in a rash and negligent manner, hit Hardeep
Singh, who was on a scooter, due to which, Hardeep
Singh died on the spot. Report was lodged by one of his
friends, who was also travelling with the deceased, based
on which FIR under Sections 279, 337 and 304 A IPC
were lodged. In fact, on 05.05.2001, charge under
Section 279, 337, 338, 427 and 304-A IPC were framed.
3. The prosecution, in order to prove its case,
examined as many as 8 witnesses, namely, PW1
Jogender Kumar, PW2 Pradeep Kumar, PW3 Mahendra
Singh, PW4 Rampal Singh Panwar, PW5 Charanjeet
Singh, PW6 Dr. Pradeep Kumar, PW7 Nootan Das and
PW8 Gaina Singh.

4
4. After prosecution evidence, the revisionist
was examined under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973. According to him, he did not hit the
deceased. The deceased hit the back-side wheel of the
bus. After hearing the parties, by the impugned
judgment, the revisionist has been convicted and
sentenced, as stated hereinbefore. The appeal was
dismissed. Hence the revision.
5. This revision has yet not been admitted.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that the revisionist would seek indulgence of the
Court on the quantum of sentence. It is submitted that
the revisionist was working with the transport
corporation; he retired on 31st of the last month;
throughout his career, except this accident, he never
was involved in any rash and negligent act; the incident
took place in the year 2000; the revisionist has already
undergone a lot of agony while facing the trial and
appeal. Therefore, he may be released on probation or
his sentence may be reduced to the sentence, which the
revisionist has already undergone.

5
7. Learned State Counsel would submit that
sentence may be reduced but the fine may be enhanced
proportionately.
8. To the limited extent of hearing on the
quantum of sentence, this revision is admitted.
9. In a criminal case, the real task begins
after conviction is recorded. Sentencing is one of the
acts, which strikes the balance between varied factors.
On the one hand, there is an offender and on the other
hand, the societal interest is also to be protected.
10. The witnesses have stated about the
manner in which the accident took place. Ex.A-4 is the
site plan, which reveals that, in fact, on a highway, this
accident took place. The FIR itself records that the
revisionist was apprehended at the spot itself. It
establishes that the revisionist did not try to run away
from the place of incident. He was on the bus. He could
have managed to leave the spot along with the bus, but
it was not done.
11. The incident took place in the year 2000. It
is stated that the applicant has now been retired and
this is the only act of negligence done by him.

6
12. Having considered the entirety of facts, this
Court is of the view that interest of justice would be
better served if the sentence is modified and the
revisionist is sentenced to 1 month simple imprisonment
under Section 279 IPC, 2 months simple imprisonment
under Section 304-A IPC, 2 months simple
imprisonment under Section 338 IPC, 2 months simple
imprisonment under Section 427 IPC and 1 month
simple imprisonment under Section 337 IPC. The fine
shall remain unaltered.
13. The revision is partly allowed. The
conviction of the revisionist is upheld.
14. The part of sentence is reduced as follows;
the revisionist is sentenced to 1 month simple
imprisonment under Section 279 IPC, 2 months simple
imprisonment under Section 304-A IPC, 2 months
simple imprisonment under Section 338 IPC, 2 months
simple imprisonment under Section 427 IPC and 1
month simple imprisonment under Section 337 IPC. The
sentences shall run concurrent. The fine shall remain
unaltered.

7
15. The impugned judgments and orders are
modified in terms of sentence as indicated hereinabove.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 15.09.2022
